subject: Private VPC integration: control-plane ↔ data-plane wiring questions

Subject: Private VPC integration: control-plane ↔ data-plane wiring questions

Hi Alex / TerraTech team,

Thanks again for walking through the topology yesterday. We're preparing the integration checklist for the first on-prem dry run and have a few questions about the control-plane ↔ data-plane interfaces so the network and security teams are aligned before cutover. High level: Redwood's control-plane (management/API) will run in the customer VPC in a private subnet with restricted egress, and the data-plane (inference pods) will live in a separate subnet with limited outbound to model artifact stores and metrics endpoints. Specific questions below — if you can answer inline that helps us finalize the runbook: 

1) mTLS termination: TerraTech mentioned terminating mTLS at the edge proxy (Gateway-01). Can you confirm whether Gateway-01 will present the client cert to downstream data-plane nodes, or if it performs re-mTLS when forwarding? If it's an L7 proxy that performs TLS passthrough, we need to ensure KV cache and streaming tokens aren't modified.

2) Control-plane health checks: our runtime makes /healthz calls to the data-plane over a short-lived control channel (port 12050). Will those be permitted between the subnets, or must they traverse the Gateway-01 host NAT?

3) SNAT/Source preservation: for audit logs we prefer source IP preservation across control-plane → data-plane calls. If SNAT is unavoidable, can TerraTech provide flow-mapping to map gateway IPs back to client identities?

4) Egress to model artifact store: data-plane needs egress to s3-compatible store (internal). The store is in an isolated VPC with a peering connection; does your recommended pattern use a proxy or a route via a dedicated egress NAT?

5) Failover path: if control-plane loses path to the primary data-plane availability zone, what are the expected DNS TTLs and BGP convergence behaviors we should account for in the runtime?

I've attached a very rough interface diagram (redwood-vpc-interface-diagram-v1.pdf) and an extract of the runbook we intend to use. If it's easier, could we schedule a 30-minute sync with your infra lead tomorrow to go line-by-line?

Next steps: please reply with short answers to the numbered items and any references to existing TerraTech ops docs.

Best,
Marcus
Principal Product Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC integration: control-plane ↔ data-plane wiring questions

Marcus — thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below (short version) and I've attached a longer ops note (tt-ops-controlplane-answers.md).

1) mTLS termination: Gateway-01 performs L7 TLS termination and then opens a new mTLS session to the data-plane (re-mTLS). We do this to enforce our edge policies. We will preserve client cert CN as an x-forwarded-client header for audit but the downstream sees a TerraTech gateway identity for the TLS session. If you require raw client certs on the data-plane we can consider TCP passthrough mode but that disables several WAF rules.

2) Control-plane health checks: /healthz (port 12050) is allowed between the subnets over the private routing fabric — it does not need to egress via NAT. We'll ensure the security groups permit the control subnet CIDR on 12050.

3) SNAT/Source preservation: we preserve source IPs when crossing the router fabric. NAT will only occur when traffic exits to public internet or when Gateway-01 forwards to an external partner. For gateway-originated flows you can map the gateway IP to an identity using our mapping table; included in the attachment.

4) Egress to artifact store: recommended pattern is route through a dedicated egress NAT host in the artifact VPC (we call it Egress-Proxy). That allows us to centralize ACLs and audit logging. We do support direct VPC peering with source IP preservation if you prefer — note that peering requires additional IAM rules for the s3-compatible endpoint.

5) Failover path: we use anycast DNS with a 30s TTL for primary endpoints and BGP sessions within the colo. Typical convergence for zonal failover is ~40-60s under events we've measured. We'll publish a short SLA note to set expectations.

Happy to run the 30-minute sync — I'm available Wed 10:00-11:30 PT. If that works we can include our infra lead (TerraTech: Priya Rao).

— Alex
Lead Site Reliability Engineer | TerraTech Solutions

Alex — thanks, that's helpful. A couple follow-ups and outcomes for our runbook: 

• Re-mTLS behavior: ok with re-mTLS but we need the gateway to inject an immutable header (x-rt-client-cn) that includes the client cert CN for end-to-end tracing. Can TerraTech make that header insertion guaranteed and documented? We will explicitly strip any header that isn't signed for security reasons, so need confirmation you'll not modify it in transit.

• Health checks: we'll add the 12050 allow rule to our security group templates. 

• SNAT mapping: please attach the mapping table to the Jira ticket (INFRA-4927) so ops can reconcile logs during cutover.

• Egress: we prefer the Egress-Proxy pattern since it gives us centralized visibility. Please send the IP ranges for Egress-Proxy so our firewall rules can be preloaded.

I've attached a small patch to the runbook (redwood-onprem-runbook-diff.txt) with the exact checklist steps we plan to execute for the dry run. Can we lock the dry-run window to Fri 3/19? If TerraTech can provide a point person (Priya) and a meeting invite I'll create the runbook cutover doc in our Drive.

Marcus / team — quick operational checklist additions for the dry-run (added to the runbook draft):

- Pre-cutover: verify TerraTech Egress-Proxy IP ranges are loaded into the perimeter ACL and our egress host accepts NATed connections.
- Validation: use curl + mTLS client cert to hit control-plane /healthz and confirm CN forwarded in x-rt-client-cn header (capture tcpdump for first 10 requests).
- Telemetry: enable debug-level metrics for 30 minutes pre/post cutover to validate KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior.
- Rollback: test redirect control-plane traffic to canary data-plane in other AZ using DNS sway (document exact steps and IAM keys).

I'll create a short checklist section with exact CLI commands. Marcus — please confirm we have authorization to request tcpdump from TerraTech gateways during the run (they may want a signed request).
